title: Sample app privacy summary (teacher-made)
subject: Computing
unit: Summer 1: Ethics and impact of computing
source: Written for computing/y9 lesson 18 (Sample app privacy summary (teacher-made))
intro: Lesson 18: Privacy, data and the law. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: SnapStudy privacy summary
paras: We collect: your name, email, date of birth, your photos, your location (always), your contacts and the time you spend in the app.
Why: to run your account, to show you adverts that match your interests and to share insights with our partners.
How long: we keep your data for as long as your account exists, and for 5 years after you delete it.
Your choices: you can turn off personalised adverts in Settings. Location can be set to 'while using the app'.

blocks.answers: Location: adverts and partners; not needed; set to never or while using. Contacts: growth and sharing; not needed; deny. Photos: only if you choose to upload notes; allow selected photos only. Time in app: adverts and design; partly; limit tracking. Keeping data 5 years after deletion goes against keeping data only as long as needed (UK GDPR).

blocks.title: Sort into: Personal data / Not personal data
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Personal data, Not personal data.
blocks.answer: Personal data: Your full name; Your location history; Your email address; Your photo. Not personal data: The weather forecast; A school's opening times

panels.title: Your rights (UK GDPR)
points: To know what data is held
To have data deleted in some cases
Data used only for a clear purpose and kept safe

keywords.def: information that identifies a living person
the UK law that controls how organisations use personal data
agreeing to data being used for a stated purpose
keeping personal information safe and used fairly

questions.q: A torch app asks for contacts and location. What do you conclude?
questions.a: It doesn't need them; refuse or choose another app.

questions.q: Evaluate a sample app privacy summary (pupil PDF): what data, why, is it needed, your verdict and settings to change.
Extend: explain why personal data is valuable to companies.
questions.a: It allows targeted advertising and product decisions.

questions.q: Under UK GDPR you have the right to ...
options: ask what data an organisation holds about you
questions.a: A) ask what data an organisation holds about you. The right of access.

questions.q: Think again: A free app is free. So how does the company make money?
questions.a: Often by collecting data and selling adverts targeted with it: 'if it's free, you may be the product'.
